title: Fitting out a meat and dairy section
target: How to set up and stock the meat and dairy section in Supermarket Simulator, given that it is a fixture of its own with goods named one by one.

steps.do: Place the section as a unit rather than lining up ordinary shelves.
steps.because: the section has a base, a collider, a left and a right door and a panel of its own (SM_Meat&Dairy, SM_Meat&Dairy_Collider, SM_Meat&Dairy_Door_l, SM_Meat&Dairy_Door_r)

steps.do: Paint the wall to match the section.
steps.because: a wall paint is named for the section, and a level-of-detail piece carries a second spelling of dairy (M_Meat&Dairy_WallPaint, SM_Meat&Diary_LOD2)

steps.do: Order the cheese by kind rather than as one line.
steps.because: a Comté, a Gruyère, a Mimolette, a mozzarella, a parmigiano and a parmesan are each named (SM_Cheese_Comté, SM_Cheese_Gruyere, SM_Cheese_Mimolette, SM_CheeseMozzarella, SM_CheeseParmigiano)

steps.do: Give the eggs and the milk their own rows.
steps.because: eggs come as a bio kind and milk under a named brand, each named on the pack as well (SM_Eggs_Bio, Eggs Bio, SM_Milk_Bourlait, Milk Bourlait)

steps.do: Do not forget the meat side of the same section.
steps.because: a ham of its own and a ham pastry stand beside the cheeses (SM_Ham_B&K, SM_Ham Pastry_Ronpoint)

steps.do: Expect the section to need cleaning.
steps.because: spilled milk has a dirt decal of its own, and the section carries its own sheets (T_Dirt_Milk_Alb, T_Meat&Dairy_Alb, T_Meat&Dairy_N)

commonMistakes: Putting cheese on a general shelf and losing the section's own display.
Buying one kind of cheese and calling the section stocked.
Leaving the wall unpainted so the section looks borrowed.
Ignoring a spill because the section is chilled rather than the floor.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
